request: Review all six actual Week10 contact sheets for layout enhancement; user finds header then image then prose too repetitive. No new artwork. GitHub is the durable store.
observations: Primary reviewer visually inspected all6 sheets. Most pages repeat title/top art/bottom prose; some tables sit on an in-world board but prose remains segregated. Sheet1 cover/OpeningDrive/scoreboard/rodeo; Sheet2 rodeo/Red soccer/central basketball/temple; Sheet3 noise/swamp delivery/SportsDesk; Sheet4 injury/birthday/battle; Sheet5 battle/reserves/transactions/standings/divisions/form; Sheet6 playoffroad/NextSix/bridgepreview/FinalWord. Six-up images are review composites, not proof of 34 native masters. The new design must preserve full prose, canonical characters, established geography, exact sports data, readability and all6 Week11 fixtures.
source_limits: You receive observations and source transcription, not image pixels. Do not claim independent visual inspection, all-team signoff, a generated fix, or mathematical elimination from chat opinion. Do not demand new research to understand the supplied creative request.

ten_questions.question: What stays recognizable across the issue without forcing every page into the same layout?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Keep type families, restrained ornaments, department labels and folio numbering; vary their placement, image scale and reading path.

ten_questions.question: Can each folio be designed around one dominant story action instead of a header–picture–paragraph stack?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Choose the dominant action before placing text: pursuit, flood, noise, delivery, reveal, resistance or decision.

ten_questions.question: Where can narration live in the scene without becoming tiny text painted onto props?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Use quiet sky, smoke, water, walls and shadow as reading space. Reserve literal signs and ledgers for short labels and exact data.

ten_questions.question: Which departments should retain the published visual language, and which can change substantially?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Preserve the Opening Drive briefing-table/map/banner identity; redesign the composition of other departments according to their distinct job.

ten_questions.question: How should three-page matchup sequences change scale and viewpoint rather than repeat a poster?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Vary establishing, active and consequence views; keep physical landmarks, screen direction, character identity and causal order fixed.

ten_questions.question: Can text and image overlap meaningfully without losing names, numbers or phone readability?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Allow selective silhouettes to cross ornamental rules, not body text; test hierarchy and contrast at phone width before color.

ten_questions.question: How can the data-heavy fifth sheet feel like the Commonwealth rather than six reports?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Give reserves, transactions, standings, divisions and scoring form different spatial structures while keeping exact data typeset and aligned.

ten_questions.question: Should The Next Six communicate why each Week 11 matchup matters, not only who plays whom?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Add source-qualified stakes beside all six full-name fixtures; distinguish top-seed pressure, potential elimination stakes and verified elimination math.

ten_questions.question: How do we build visual rhythm across all 34 pages instead of adding decoration to each one?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Alternate dense and spacious folios; use scenic transitions and the Final Word as breathing room, with shared typography rather than identical bands.

ten_questions.question: What must the next proof demonstrate before we approve production?
ten_questions.proposed_direction: Exact portrait page geometry, actual canonical image references, complete copy, accurate source-bound data, non-repetitive reading paths and scaled-sheet fidelity.
